knowledgeAnswers.rationale: Brushing an internal duct reaches a concealed part of the system and is outside the routine boundary. Being part of the same system, or client agreement in conversation, does not make it routine or eligible.
The method boundary is set by the written scope, the site procedure and the approved product list. Experience and available tools do not set it.
The request is recorded, the specialist method is declined, and it is referred. A quick trial or a quote before written scope and eligibility are in place is not correct.

practicalCriteria: Classifies five sample methods as routine or specialist, with a stated reason for each, and marks any unclear method as specialist until the site confirms it.
Declines a simulated specialist method request without offering a partial version, and writes a referral that names the person who can approve a change of scope.
Checks the safety data sheet of a sample product for handling, dilution, ventilation and disposal before use, and records the product reference.
passRule: All five methods classified with reasons, the specialist request declined and referred with no partial work offered, and the product check recorded. Observed in a supervised desk exercise. A pass is not a method approval and does not confer any licence or specialist authority.
evidenceRequired: Method classification record for the five sample methods
Referral record for the simulated specialist request
Safety data sheet check record for the sample product
stopWorkCriteria: Access point opened or internal duct touched on a routine-method assumption
Degreaser or sanitiser used without checking its safety data sheet or the approved list
Specialist method offered, quoted or partly performed without written scope and eligibility
